title: The 'or' binary operator is slow: MetricName comparison reallocates strings inside a nested per-series loop

source.license_note: Real upstream victoria optimization PR #8489; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up the PromQL 'or' binary operator by removing redundant per-iteration MetricName string allocations and comparisons in fillLeftNaNsWithRightValuesOrMerge.
task.instructions: Optimize the app/vmselect/promql package for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark BenchmarkBinaryOpOr measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: fillLeftNaNsWithRightValuesOrMerge calls MetricName.String() for every left/right series pair inside a nested loop, allocating a fresh string each iteration and lacking a scalar fast path.

ops_fault.description: Profiling of 'a or b' queries shows the 'or' operator dominated by MetricName.String() allocations in fillLeftNaNsWithRightValuesOrMerge.
detection_keywords: GC pressure from per-iteration string allocation
repair_keywords: add scalar fast path via isScalar to skip MetricName comparison
marshalMetricNameSorted into pooled bbPool byte buffers
compare with bytes.Equal instead of MetricName.String()
hoist nameLeft marshaling out of inner loop
avoid per-iteration string allocation, reuse buffers

visible_context.issue_text: Queries using the 'or' binary operator (e.g. 'a or b') became significantly slower after v1.111.0; CPU profiles point at MetricName comparison work when filling left NaNs with right values.
error_logs: pprof: 71% cpu in promql.fillLeftNaNsWithRightValuesOrMerge -> storage.(*MetricName).String -> runtime.mallocgc (string alloc per series pair)
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization; profiling diagnosis injected as upstream context.
